_comment: COMMITTED, and must stay NON-SECRET. Every secret (Jwt:PrivateKeyPem, Jwt:RefreshTokenHmacKeyPlain, Gateway tokens, real SMTP or OAuth credentials) belongs in appsettings.Development.local.json beside this file, which is git-ignored and is where the API writes the keys it generates on first run. A fresh clone should need no edits here: `dotnet run` generates its own keys into the .local file.
_secret_comment: Development is stated explicitly rather than inheriting the Certificate default from appsettings.json: no developer has the Data Protection certificate, so Certificate mode would abort startup. The code in AuthDataProtectionExtensions.ResolveStorageMode falls back the same way, but that is a safety net — this line is the actual contract, and it keeps Development independent of Production's default.

Jwt._comment: Keys are NOT here: they are generated into appsettings.Development.local.json on first run.

Gateway._comment: Gateway token validation is off locally, so the API is reachable without running the gateway. The generated token itself lands in the .local file.

Email._comment: Disabled by default; point SmtpHost/SmtpPort at a local catcher (e.g. Papercut, MailHog on 1025) and set Enabled=true to exercise mail. Real credentials, if ever needed, go in the .local file.

ExternalAuth._comment: Placeholder client id. Put a real one in the .local file - it is not a secret, but it is machine-specific.

_idp_comment: Both URLs are https on purpose. PublicBaseUrl MUST be the exact origin the SPA is built against (VITE_API_BASE_URL): the authorize endpoint builds returnTo from it, and getValidReturnTo in packages/auth rejects any other origin as an open-redirect attempt - so a mismatch drops the post-login resume silently. Run the API on the `https` launch profile.

Cors._comment: 5173 = console, 5174 = accounts (each app's vite.config.ts pins its port). Both schemes stay listed: the dev servers fall back to http when DEV_HTTPS_CERT/DEV_HTTPS_KEY are unset. Listed in full because a shorter override list does not truncate this one.

ImageStorage._comment: Absolute PublicBaseUrl so the Vite SPAs can load images from the API. https to match them: an http image on an https page is mixed content, which Chrome upgrades to https://localhost:5100 - where nothing listens - so every avatar and logo would break.
